stories.label: U.S. approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
stories.summary: The State Department approved a $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot missiles while Zelensky says deliveries are running late and Russian strikes cut power in Kyiv and elsewhere overnight. Lead with the gap between an approval and a missile in a launcher: who is left exposed while the munition is scarce, and who else competes for the same stock during the Iran war, as far as the sources say. One source says 'systems'; the figure is 500 missiles per the headline and the other reports, so check it. Al Jazeera and Hindustan Times carry the non-US framing. Dateline Kyiv, where it lands; not a US pick.

stories.label: Iran's Khamenei Orders Military to Expand US Retaliation Plans
stories.summary: New development: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei told commanders that any US or Israeli attack must be met immediately and with a wider geographic reach, as speculation grows that the war will resume after the US midterms. Lead with the order and what 'geographic' expansion would put in range, and who lives there: Gulf states, shipping, the neighbours whose security chiefs were in Tehran days ago. Keep it his stated order, not a demonstrated capability. Bloomberg and Dawn are the independent reports; TRT World and TASS are state media and are attributed if used. Do not repeat the Hormuz talks entry. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Iran agrees to reopen Strait of Hormuz within two days if deal reached with US
stories.summary: New development in the Qatari mediation: TASS reports Foreign Minister Araghchi saying Iran has agreed to shorten its timeline for reopening the strait to two days if a deal is reached, while demanding recognition of the route it discussed with Oman and the closure of the others. Lead with the condition, not the promise: Iran would reopen the strait on terms that make it a co-owner of the route. A second TASS report says an Iranian delegation is in Doha examining mediators' nuclear proposals, citing Araghchi to Al Jazeera: https://tass.com/world/2211371. No independent source is in the feed, so attribute everything to Russian state news agency TASS and state nothing as fact. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Doha.

stories.label: Pantanal entra oficialmente na rota da aridez, aponta plano do governo
stories.summary: A Brazilian government plan now officially places the Pantanal, the vast wetland, on the path to aridity, and scientists say the country must change how it produces food and runs cattle. Lead with the state's own document saying this about a wetland. The accountability question: who holds the land, who drove the change according to the source, and whether the plan binds anyone or only records the loss. Give the people who live from it their weight. Dateline the place the source reports from, in Brazil, as a city.

stories.label: Shipping Strikes In Hormuz Leave Both Sides With Economic Pain
stories.summary: The National reports that attacks on ships transiting Hormuz in October were the highest of any month since the war began. Lead with that count, then the standoff it produces: the US blockade has cut off Iran's oil exports and a key part of its military funding, while Iran's intermittent strikes keep raising the cost for everyone else. New beyond last cycle's single-tanker and Brent stories: the month's tally and who is losing what. Name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Khasab unless the sources place the lead elsewhere.

stories.label: Russia extends diesel export ban through January, allows limited shipments By Investing.com
stories.summary: Russia extended its general ban on diesel exports by domestic producers through the end of January, with exemptions for some suppliers, to hold its home fuel market steady. Lead with the decision and who loses the barrels abroad, in a market already short because of Hormuz. The mechanism: on the same day Ukrainian drones hit the Bashneft refineries in Ufa, after reports that Kyiv had paused refinery strikes under US pressure over diesel prices (Bloomberg, a teaser only: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-31/ukraine-strikes-bashneft-refineries-as-russia-attacks-power-grid). Say who is exempt if the source does. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Power bills and data centres cast rare spotlight on utilities in US midterms
stories.summary: Electricity prices, usually invisible in US national elections, are a campaign issue days before the midterms, as voters resent rising bills and deals for power-hungry data centres. Lead with the Energy Information Administration price rise and who pays for the AI build-out: households, on a grid being rebuilt for tech companies. Name the mechanism by which the cost reaches the bill, and the races where it counts, Ohio among them if the source says. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline the city the source leads from.

stories.label: 透视A股三季报：AI算力领跑，材料量价齐升，地产和消费寻底｜看财报
stories.summary: A mainland reading of China's listed companies' third-quarter results: AI computing leads, materials are rising in both volume and price, while property and consumption are still looking for a floor. Lead with the split inside the same economy and the figures that show it: who earns from the state-backed compute build, and what the weak property and consumer lines say about Chinese households. Do not write it as a market recap. The view is TMTPost's own, and attributed as such. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: AI-based attendance system leads to dismissal of 72 doctors in Balochistan
stories.summary: Balochistan's Health Department dismissed 72 doctors from government service for prolonged absence, under an AI-based attendance system the province introduced to make medical staff report for duty. Lead with an algorithm's record ending 72 government careers in one of Pakistan's most underserved provinces. The two questions: patients in clinics where a doctor drew a salary and did not appear, and what recourse a doctor has if the system is wrong. Say what the system actually does and who checked its findings, as far as Dawn does. Dateline Quetta.

stories.label: Verhaltensscanner in Berlin: Kreisverkehr der Kontrolle
stories.summary: Automated round-the-clock behaviour scanning began last week at Kottbusser Tor in Berlin: 30 cameras and software that continuously checks whether everyone present behaves as wanted, in a place where homeless people also sleep. Lead with the system at work on the people who cannot leave the frame. The precedent is the point: what the software flags, who sees it, under what law, and how the place has changed in a week, as netzpolitik.org reports it. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: AI如何赋能企业研发？快手团队提出“臭鼬工厂”模式
stories.summary: Kuaishou's own engineers put a number on the limit of AI coding: development is about 20% of end-to-end delivery, so making code ten times faster improves delivery only about 22%. Lead with that arithmetic and its consequence: the bottleneck moves to verification, and Kuaishou is reorganising into small teams to remove coordination rather than add tools. OPPO at the same forum says it once required staff to hit a monthly token quota. The 133% throughput and 79% cycle-time claims are the company's own figures from a company salon, and are attributed as such. Not the Kling funding story. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: The FDA wants to pull its approval of a drug. It's not so easy.
stories.summary: The FDA says Tavneos, a drug for a rare autoimmune vasculitis that damages organs, was approved on manipulated study data, and is trying to withdraw it, while patients already depend on it. Lead with the regulator's claim and the bind it creates: what a withdrawal does to the people taking it, and why revoking an approval is harder than granting one. Keep manipulation the FDA's allegation, and give Amgen's response if the source does. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline Washington unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
stories.summary: The United States, hosting the G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta, scrapped the traditional group photo after European officials refused to be pictured with Russia's Sergey Lavrov. Lead with what the lost photo shows: the host and its allies cannot share a frame, so ask what the meeting can actually decide on Ukraine and the Iran war. Give the non-Western voices their weight: India's Jaishankar told the plenary that military solutions are not working (Hindustan Times: https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/military-solutions-not-working-give-diplomacy-a-chance-jaishankar-at-g20-101793388929402.html; NDTV: https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/us-bins-g20-photo-as-europeans-object-to-posing-with-russias-lavrov-12262024). US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Atlanta.

stories.label: Leaders grapple with finance and harmful subsidies at UN's COP17 biodiversity conference
stories.summary: Nearly 200 nations struck agreements on Friday at the UN biodiversity summit in Yerevan, with deep divisions left over funding, harmful subsidies and scientific priorities. Lead with what was signed against what was missed: who pays for conservation, and which subsidies that damage nature survive. The mechanism: countries holding most of the remaining biodiversity need money that the richer states have not committed. Name who blocked what. Mongabay is the independent report; TRT World is Turkish state media and is attributed if used. Dateline Yerevan.

stories.label: Rival US and Russian resolutions on Western Sahara fail at UN
stories.summary: The Security Council rejected competing US and Russian resolutions, leaving the UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara without an approved extension. Lead with the mission and the people it exists for: the Sahrawis, promised a referendum they have never held, and Morocco's claim to the territory. Say what each draft proposed, who voted how, and what happens to the mission when its mandate runs out. The mechanism: two powers fighting over the wording can end a mission neither of them depends on. Dateline Laayoune, where the mission is based, unless the source places the lead elsewhere.

stories.label: EXCLUSIVE: Report details NSCDC officers' contributions to detention tragedy in Niger, recommends dismissal, prosecution
stories.summary: New development on the 33 detainees who died in NSCDC custody in Minna, covered 30 October through the compensation proposal: Premium Times has the panel's findings, that senior officers authorised operations without clearance, ignored warnings of possible suffocation and failed to intervene, with dismissal and prosecution recommended. Lead with what the officers were warned of and what they did, naming them only as the report does and stating that these are a panel's findings, not a conviction. The accountability question: whether the government acts on prosecution, or stops at paying the families. Dateline Minna.

stories.label: Prime suspect in Gujranwala bride's murder killed in alleged exchange of fire, claims CCD
stories.summary: Punjab's Crime Control Department says the prime suspect in the wedding-day murder of a bride in Gujranwala died in an alleged exchange of fire after he was traced to Karachi. Lead with the death of a suspect before any trial, and keep it the department's claim, as Dawn does. Name the bride if the source does. The mechanism: when a killing ends a case, no court tests the evidence or the police account. Give any figures the source or the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan offers on such encounters, and nothing beyond them. Dateline Lahore.

stories.label: BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi Slams Congress Over Mock Parliament Session
stories.summary: The feed's headline is the political row; the story is the World Bank figure beneath it, from the Bloomberg link. About 496 million Indians were lifted above the $4.20-a-day line between 2011 and 2023, one of the fastest declines recorded, while the share below that line fell from 57.7%. Lead with the number and then who was left out, because the gains are uneven: by state, caste, religion or sex, as far as the report says. Say what $4.20 buys, and how the BJP is already using the figure against Congress (Economic Times). Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Rating agency Fitch hits France with surprise outlook downgrade
stories.summary: Fitch moved France's outlook to negative in a surprise decision, hours after data showed the economy unexpectedly shrank in the third quarter. Lead with the two blows on one day. The mechanism: a shrinking economy cuts the revenue that services the debt, so borrowing costs rise just as the European Central Bank debates raising rates in response to the Iran war's energy shock. Who pays: French taxpayers and whoever loses out in the next budget. Follows Thursday's ECB and French bonds story. Name the ECB deposit rate and the euro. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Claude官宣取消5小时限额！ChatGPT负责人：最好宣布28天重置期
stories.summary: The headline is a subscription change: Anthropic is lifting the five-hour usage limit on its $200 plan, a day after OpenAI doubled allowances. The story is the money beneath it. Zhidx reports that Anthropic's S-1, filed 26 October, shows first-half 2026 revenue of $16.286 billion against a net loss of $80.748 billion, with a listing targeted for the week of 16 November, and relays the FT's report that it expects a double-B, junk-grade rating after the IPO, against Blackstone's earlier forecast of investment grade by 2027. Lead with the loss set against the revenue, say how much of it is non-cash if the filing is available, and attribute the rating to the FT as relayed. The mechanism: price cuts to hold users while borrowing gets costlier. Follows the OpenAI fundraising story from the last cycle; do not repeat it. Treat this company as any other. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: Surface-To-Air Missiles Deployed To Protect Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Estate
stories.summary: Avenger launchers firing Stinger missiles, with counter-drone sensor and jammer kits from US Northern Command, now guard the US president's Florida estate. Lead with the hardware: a battlefield air-defence system on American soil around a private residence. The mechanism: cheap drones have made low-altitude air defence a homeland problem, and the fly-away kits show how the military is answering it. Say what threat the source gives, and do not supply one, including from the Iran war, if it does not. Say what it costs if the source does. US pick 3 of 3. Dateline Palm Beach.

stories.label: “开源才是护城河”：制造老炮把品胜的AI交给了00后
stories.summary: A view from inside China's tech press: Zhao Guocheng, a manufacturing veteran at the accessories maker Pisen, has handed its AI work to a team led by Cong Zelong, born after 2000, on the argument that open source is the moat. Lead with what that team has actually built and shipped, and what it does to the factory's productivity. The mechanism: open models let an ordinary hardware maker build AI without a lab's budget, which is how much of Chinese industry is adopting it. Report facts, attribute judgments to TMTPost, and do not write a company profile. Dateline where the source places the company.

stories.label: 押注睡着的8小时，前小米王腾闯入千亿AI睡眠赛道
stories.summary: Wang Teng, formerly of Xiaomi, has entered what TMTPost calls a market worth hundreds of billions of yuan: AI for sleep. Lead with the product and the money behind it, and what it collects. The stake for the reader: a device watching the eight hours a person is unconscious, so ask what happens to that data and what claims it makes about health, as far as the source supports. Attribute the market size to TMTPost and say if the product has shown evidence that it works. Dateline where the source places the company.

stories.label: Scientists think our recent ancestors may have run hotter -- but why?
stories.summary: Average human body temperature appears to have been higher 150 years ago than it is now, which unsettles the 37C figure Carl Wunderlich set in the 1860s. Lead with the size of the drop and the studies that measured it, then the live explanations, such as fewer chronic infections. Be plain about what is measured and what is still argued, including whether old thermometers explain it. Why it matters: fever is judged against a norm that may no longer hold. Name the studies and the researchers. Dateline where the source places the lead researchers.

stories.label: Aid convoy enters besieged Ukrainian town Oleshky
stories.summary: Hundreds of civilians left Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday in a four-hour window, under a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, and some stayed behind. Lead with the people and the clock: who got out, who remained and why, and what the siege had left them without. The mechanism: civilian survival in a besieged town depended on a four-hour pause arranged from outside, so ask what happens to those still there once it closes. The BBC link is a video page; Al Jazeera and Ukrainska Pravda carry the text. Give Russian and Ukrainian accounts, attributed. Dateline Oleshky.

stories.label: US execution survivor Christa Pike says she is now in 'constant pain'
stories.summary: Tennessee tried to execute Christa Pike by lethal injection and failed; she is alive, 50, in solitary confinement and in what she calls constant pain, with no settled answer on what the state does next. Lead with her first statement and the state's position: a government that attempted a killing and did not finish it. India TV says two injections were attempted, so check that against the other sources and state it only if confirmed. State her crime and name her victim plainly, as a matter of equal weight. The accountability question: who answers for how the execution failed, and can Tennessee try again. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Nashville unless the sources place the prison elsewhere.

stories.label: Man sets himself ablaze outside court after daughter's 'rapist' acquitted in Lahore
stories.summary: Allah Bakhshaya set himself on fire outside the Muzaffargarh district courts on Friday after the man accused of raping his daughter was acquitted, nine years into the case. Lead with the nine years. The mechanism: a family that went to the courts waited most of a decade for a verdict, and the wait itself is the accusation against the system. Say why the court acquitted, if the source gives it, and his condition as reported. The accused was acquitted, so do not call him a rapist, and do not identify the daughter. Give any figures the source has on delay or conviction in such cases, and nothing more. The headline says Lahore, the event was in Muzaffargarh. Dateline Muzaffargarh.

stories.label: China's Factory Activity Slips as New Export Orders Weaken
stories.summary: China's factory activity slipped as new export orders weakened, on the same day Premier Li Qiang told Germany's visiting President Steinmeier that China is willing to import more German goods. Lead with the factory reading and the export orders, from the U.S. News report, then set Li's offer against it: the world's workshop is short of foreign buyers while promising to buy more itself. The mechanism: protectionism between Europe and Beijing is closing the outlet Chinese factories depend on. Say who is exposed first, in China's export towns and in Germany's industry. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: OpenAI reportedly cuts fundraising target amid AI jitters
stories.summary: OpenAI has cut the capital raise and valuation it was seeking, the FT reported late Friday: it had been after $30 billion at $1.4 trillion and has put off its IPO to 2027. Lead with the old number and the new one. The mechanism: AI companies spend ahead of revenue and depend on the next round, so a stock sell-off reaches them as a higher cost of staying alive. The same day the FT reported that Anthropic expects a double-B, junk-grade credit rating after its IPO (Zhidx: https://zhidx.com/p/606194.html), which shows the same pressure on debt, if the writer can confirm it. Keep figures attributed to the FT as relayed. This follows Friday's Amazon capital-spending story; say what changed. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: Trump's tariffs could shut this Canadian town. Its residents are fighting to save it
stories.summary: Témiscaming, Quebec, was built around a paper mill a century ago, and the mill now sits idle after US-Canada trade talks broke down. Lead with the town and what the mill's closure takes with it: jobs, tax base and the reason the place exists. The mechanism: a tariff set in Washington lands on a single-employer town with nothing to fall back on, far from anyone who decided it. Say how many jobs, who owns the mill, what residents are doing to save it, and what Ottawa has offered. This is the human cost of the trade break covered Friday, not the Montreal summit. Dateline Témiscaming.

stories.label: 198亿到账！AI视频最大单笔融资诞生
stories.summary: Kuaishou told the Hong Kong exchange on 30 October that the funding of its video-generation business Kling has closed at about 19.8 billion yuan ($2.9 billion), which Zhidx calls the largest single round in AI video. Lead with the amount and who holds what: Kuaishou's Lucky Labs keeps 66.68%, CEO Gai Kun holds 3.02% of the equity but 23.72% of the votes, and Alibaba, Tencent and Baidu hold small stakes, with Beijing state funds among the backers announced in July. Two investors failed to pay in full and left the deal, which is worth a line. The mechanism: rival platforms and the state pay together to fund a Chinese video model. Kling's second-quarter revenue passed 850 million yuan. Attribute the 'largest' claim to Zhidx. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: ISRO successfully launches NVS-03 satellite to strengthen India's NavIC navigation system, improve civilian access
stories.summary: ISRO launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite on a GSLV on Friday, and its chairman Narayanan says it flew with its pyro valves open to overcome a technical hurdle. Lead with that workaround: how an agency changed a satellite's flight configuration to get past a known problem, and what the earlier problem cost. The stake is who controls positioning: NavIC is India's way of not depending on GPS or BeiDou, in war and for civilian phones, so say how many working satellites the system now has against how many it needs. Dateline Sriharikota.

stories.label: DOJ raises privacy concerns over potential sale of Character.AI chats
stories.summary: The Justice Department's Executive Office for US Trustees says a consumer privacy ombudsman is needed to advise the court on what Character.AI data can be sold and on what terms. Lead with what is on the block: conversations people had with a companion chatbot, treated as an asset in a sale. The mechanism: a promise made to users at sign-up may not bind whoever buys the company, and a court now decides. Say who the seller and bidders are, whether minors' chats are included, and what users can do, as far as the source supports. A thin feed entry, picked because no other outlet in the feed has it. US pick 3 of 3. Dateline Washington unless the source places the court elsewhere.

stories.label: A New Map of ‘Empty’ Space Challenges a Tranquil Picture of the Galaxy
stories.summary: Astronomers long treated the interstellar medium, the gas and dust between the stars, as a static backdrop; 3D mapping now shows it in motion. Lead with what the maps show that the old picture could not, and why it matters: this medium is what stars form from. Name the surveys and researchers behind the maps, and say what remains unsettled. Dateline where the source places the lead researchers.

stories.label: Police deployed during stand-off over control of Poland's top court
stories.summary: Police entered the premises of Poland's Constitutional Tribunal and its president was suspended; President Nawrocki turned his plane back mid-flight to Senegal to return. Lead with police inside a top court, an EU member's constitutional fight turned physical. Say who ordered what, on what legal claim, and who was detained. The mechanism: Tusk's government and the Law and Justice-aligned presidency each dispute who lawfully holds the court, so whoever controls it can rule on the other. Dateline Warsaw.

stories.label: DOJ official calls allegations about 2 Dan Sullivans in Alaska Senate race "troubling," but focus of probe is unclear
stories.summary: New development on the ballot row covered 28 October: US Attorney Michael Heyman reports a 'significant surge of law enforcement assets' to Alaska, and the Justice Department has asked for a preliminary injunction, days before the vote. Lead with federal agents and a court request arriving in a tight Senate race, and be plain that the probe's focus is unclear. The accountability question runs both ways: who recruited the second Dan Sullivan, and what it means when a president who demanded a candidate's prosecution sees his Justice Department move in the final week. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Anchorage.

stories.label: Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer accused of running over man in Houston
stories.summary: A Harris County grand jury indicted an ICE officer accused of deliberately striking a fleeing Mexican construction worker with an SUV during an immigration raid. Lead with the charge and the man it was done to, named if the source names him. The structural point is rarity: a local prosecutor charging a federal immigration officer, and whether federal immunity arguments can take the case away from a Texas court. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline Houston.

stories.label: Thousands of people in Gaza are missing without answers, as Israel withholds information from their families
stories.summary: More than a year after the October 2025 ceasefire, Palestinian families are still searching for relatives who vanished, and Israel withholds what it knows. Lead with the families and the names the report gives. The mechanism: without a death record or a detention record a person is neither mourned nor visited, and the one party holding the records does not have to answer. Give the count and who made it. A thin feed entry, picked because no other outlet in the feed reports it. Dateline Gaza City, or where the source places the families.

stories.label: No solo la milpa: lo que la crisis climática se llevó en los territorios indígenas de Honduras y Guatemala
stories.summary: The 2026 El Niño drought, intensified by climate change, took the maize harvest from Maya Ch'orti' families in Jocotán, Guatemala, and Lenca families in La Paz and Intibucá, Honduras. Lead with what is lost beyond the crop: no harvest means no native seed saved from their ancestors, so next year's planting goes too. Health workers describe sadness, anxiety and hopelessness that these communities face alone. Ask what either state has provided, and name who emits and who pays. Dateline Jocotán.

stories.label: Highlights From North Korea’s Drone-A-Palooza
stories.summary: Pyongyang put a growing arsenal of reconnaissance and attack drones on display, including a stealthy combat drone concept the source calls very aspirational. Lead with what is plausibly operational against what is only a model, keeping that line clear. Say what the display suggests about where the designs and the battlefield experience come from, only as far as the source supports, and what it means for South Korea. Dateline Pyongyang.

stories.label: Limpet mine attack in Hormuz suggests Iran may be shifting tactics
stories.summary: New development on the tanker attack covered this afternoon: security sources now tell Reuters the UAE-owned crude tanker was hit by limpet mines, the first successful such attack on a commercial ship in the Middle East since 2019, which undercuts the Pentagon's claim to have fully cleared and opened the strait. Lead with that gap between the claim and the hull. Set it against the IRGC Navy's statement that tankers on 'unauthorised routes' met incidents, attributed as Iranian state media, and Oman's rescue of 25 crew. The Iranian role is reported, not proven, so attribute it. Who pays: the crews, insurers, then fuel importers. The War Zone (https://www.twz.com/news-features/iran-used-limpet-mine-placed-on-ships-hull-in-latest-strait-of-hormuz-attack-report) reports more US forces flowing into the region. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Dateline Khasab.

stories.label: Telesat Stays Quiet on C$2.4B GEO Debt Due in December
stories.summary: Telesat owes C$2.4 billion on its legacy geostationary business in December, and its CEO told analysts he is 'pretty constrained' in what he can say about refinancing. Lead with the deadline and the silence. The mechanism: the old satellite business carrying the debt is shrinking while Canada's bet on a non-Starlink network, Lightspeed, depends on the same company. Say who holds the debt and how public money is exposed, if the source supports it. Dateline Ottawa.

stories.label: 具身智能患上了焦虑症
stories.summary: A view from inside China's own tech press: investment in humanoid and embodied-AI robots is cooling from frenzy to caution. Lead with the numbers the piece gives on money, valuations or orders. The mechanism: a sector financed by venture and state capital on promise now has to show paying customers beyond demonstrations. This follows this week's Hong Kong listing and order stories, so say what has changed for investors, not the robots. Report the facts, and attribute judgments to TMTPost. Dateline Beijing unless the source says otherwise.

stories.label: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
stories.summary: An official extension for Anthropic's Claude, on a verified Cursor account, carried a backdoor for nearly 12 hours, threatening as many as 5,000 developers' machines, and Ars reports Anthropic had not yet warned customers. Lead with the window and the silence. The mechanism: developers install a verified publisher's extension with access to their machine and credentials, so one stolen account reaches them all at once. How the attackers got in is unknown; say so. Say what affected developers should do, and include any company response the source carries. US pick 3 of 3. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: Stealthy GJ-21 Drone Has Launched And Recovered From Type 076 Amphibious Assault Ship, China Claims
stories.summary: China claims its stealthy GJ-21 combat drone has launched from and landed on the Type 076 amphibious assault ship, the milestone the ship was built for. Lead with that, attributed as China's claim. The mechanism: catapult and arresting gear on a smaller deck give an amphibious ship carrier-like reach without pilots or a full carrier's cost, which changes the sums around Taiwan and the South China Sea. Say what remains unverified. Dateline Shanghai unless the source says otherwise.

stories.label: When chatbots become ‘answer engines’: AI, geopolitics and truth
stories.summary: Research from Kosovo tests how AI chatbots present contested geopolitics, and finds them sometimes distorting it. Lead with a specific answer the researchers recorded, and which chatbots gave it. The mechanism: a small state's history is thinly documented in English, so a model repeats whichever side wrote the most, and readers get one answer with no sources to weigh. Say how the study was done and how far it can be generalised. Dateline Pristina.

stories.label: Internet Governance Forum 2026: Lebanon Discusses Digital Recovery as Reforms Remain Stalled
stories.summary: At the Internet Governance Forum in Beirut, officials promised digital transformation and AI governance while Lebanon's infrastructure crumbles and its data and privacy protections remain ineffective. Lead with one concrete gap the report names between promise and law. Who is affected: Lebanese whose records sit in state systems with no effective protection, in a country still recovering from war. Name the stalled reforms and who is responsible for them. Dateline Beirut.

stories.label: Uttarakhand Chopper Horror: 13 Mishaps, 21 Deaths In 10 Years
stories.summary: A helicopter carrying five pilgrims from Badrinath to Dehradun crashed near Joshimath in bad weather, the latest in a run of crashes on Uttarakhand's pilgrim routes. Lead with the crash and the pattern, then ask who lets these flights go up in Himalayan weather and what the regulator did after the earlier crashes. Pilgrims pay for a booming shuttle trade and the state promotes it. State the toll as officials give it. The outlets disagree on the ten-year count: Hindustan Times says 21 deaths and NDTV 27, so reconcile them or say so. Dateline Joshimath.

stories.label: Italy tightens security as students, unions launch nationwide protests
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of students and union members marched in dozens of Italian cities on Friday over living costs, education spending and the wars in the Middle East, and the government answered by tightening security. Lead with the scale and what joins these demands: a war-driven rise in prices and a government spending elsewhere. Name who called the action and what they want from the Meloni government. Mention today's dockworkers' strike over Gaza only if the source links the two. Dateline Rome.

stories.label: Yemen’s War Has Turned Facebook Into a Mourning Wall
stories.summary: As fighting intensified this fall, Yemenis turned Facebook into a running record of the dead, and hundreds of posts trace the lives of students and graduates who felt they had no choice but to take up arms. Lead with the names and lives the source gives: the war's dead counted by their own families because no one else is counting. The mechanism: a collapsed economy leaves young graduates with a rifle as the only wage. Say who recruits them and what the warring sides have published about their losses. Dateline in Yemen, where the source places it.

stories.label: Pacific ‘Pre-COP’ draws attention to islands’ plight
stories.summary: Pacific island states hosted the talks before COP31, and the harder test comes next month in Turkey: turning attention into commitments on the ocean. Lead with what the island governments asked for and what they actually got, treating them as negotiators, not victims. The mechanism: the states least responsible for emissions hold moral weight but little leverage over the large emitters. Say which commitments are on paper and who has declined to make them. Dateline where the pre-COP met, as the source gives it.

stories.label: Record-High Heating Oil Prices Are Closing Argument in Maine Senate Race
stories.summary: The Iran war has pushed Maine's heating oil to record prices days before a Senate election, in a state where many homes heat with oil. Lead with what a household now pays to fill a tank as winter starts: the bill for a war 10,000km away, landing on people with no way to switch fuel. Then the vote: how Collins and Jackson each answer for it. Keep the political framing attributed to Drop Site. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Maine, in the city the source names.

stories.label: Brent crude price rises by nearly 2.5% on ICE exchange
stories.summary: Brent crude rose more than 2% on Friday and is heading for a fourth straight monthly gain, after a tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz and Washington again raised the possibility of renewing hostilities with Iran. Lead with the fourth month, not the day: how far Brent crude has climbed since the run began. The mechanism: a price set by the risk of crossing one strait, and by a threat from one government. Who pays: fuel-importing economies and their poorest buyers. Name Brent crude and WTI. Attribute anything from TASS to Russian state media. Dateline Dubai.

stories.label: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
stories.summary: New development on this morning's story: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng says the investigation found further breach points beyond the employee laptop first suspected, and he set Sunday as the target to restore withdrawals (CoinDesk: https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/10/30/binance-uncovers-wider-breach-in-usd6-3-billion-exploit-targets-sunday-withdrawal-restart). Lead with the wider breach and the date. Customers' money stays locked until a company that does not yet know how far the attackers reached says it is safe. About $3bn is secured and the rest is not. Keep the North Korea link attributed, and name bitcoin.

stories.label: OPay lists on NYSE, raises $304m in IPO at $4 billion valuation
stories.summary: OPay raised $304 million at a $4 billion valuation, the first major Nigeria-focused fintech to list on a US exchange. Lead with where the listing happened: a company built on Nigerian savers and market traders sells its shares in New York, not Lagos. Say who owns it and who gains from the float, how many Nigerians use it, and what the naira means for dollar investors in a business that earns in naira. Name the naira. Dateline Lagos.

stories.label: Ogra notifies 15.3pc increase in RLNG price for October
stories.summary: Pakistan's regulator has raised the price of regasified LNG by up to 15.3% for October, mainly because of higher crude prices. Lead with the size of the rise and how fast a war abroad reaches a Pakistani gas bill, because the imported fuel's price follows Brent crude. Say who buys RLNG (power plants, industry, the Sui companies' customers) and what it means for electricity and factory costs. Different from yesterday's quarterly-pricing bill and the diesel rise: this is the decision itself. Name natural gas prices and Brent crude. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Fujifilm to boost tape production 5x as AI fuels archiving demand
stories.summary: Fujifilm will invest about 10 billion yen ($63 million) to multiply its magnetic tape capacity fivefold, because of AI data. Lead with the surprise: the newest computing boom is reviving a storage medium from the 1950s. The mechanism is cost and security: tape is cheap, and a cartridge sitting offline cannot be reached by an attacker. Say what is being archived and who is buying it. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: Analysts find looming launch crisis is "more severe" than anticipated
stories.summary: Quilty Space reports that outside China the world faces a significant shortage of rockets through 2030, and there is no evidence Starship will carry traditional satellites. Lead with the size of the gap. The mechanism: one company's Falcon 9 carries most of the West's payloads while its rivals run late, so countries wanting their own satellites have to queue for a seat with SpaceX or go to China. Say who gets left waiting, including smaller states. Dateline where the source places the firm, and keep the figures attributed to Quilty.

stories.label: Scientists Analyzed Thousands of Psychedelic Trips. They Found Something Disturbing
stories.summary: A newly released database of more than 25,000 anonymized calls to the Fireside Project's Psychedelic Support Line shows what happens outside the clinic, where the drugs' promising trial results were not measured. Lead with the disturbing finding itself, stated exactly as the researchers measured it, and be plain that callers to a crisis line are not a sample of all users. The gap to explain: enthusiasm rests on supervised trials, while most use has no supervision. Name the study and journal if the source does. US pick 2 of 3.

stories.label: Russia's last major independent newspaper shuts under government pressure
stories.summary: Novaya Gazeta, the Nobel-winning paper that lost Anna Politkovskaya and other reporters to murder, says it is winding up its remaining operations after a campaign of state pressure in which a senior editor has been prosecuted. Lead with the closure and what the state actually did to force it. The mechanism: no ban was needed, only prosecutions and pressure, so name each tool used. Say what remains of independent Russian reporting, most of it now in exile. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: UK maritime agency reports fire aboard vessel in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: New development on the Hormuz attacks covered 29 October: the UK's UKMTO centre says a small boat approached a tanker and attached two explosive devices to its hull, and the blasts set the engine room on fire. Lead with that method: a boat crew placing charges by hand is a different act from the sea mines the IRGC described for this week's tanker blasts, and it means someone chose this ship. Attribute through UKMTO and say TRT World, Turkish state media, carried it; say plainly if no one has claimed it or blamed anyone. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude, which traded near $113.51 a barrel on Friday by TASS's reading of ICE data. Who pays: the crews, then every fuel-importing economy. Dateline Khasab.

stories.label: What can a global strike of dockworkers achieve for Gaza?
stories.summary: More than 25 dockworkers' unions in over 110 ports across 22 countries strike today over Gaza. Report the strike, not the feature's question: lead with the scale, and say which ports and what cargo they are refusing. The mechanism: arms reach a war through a few chokepoints in ordinary ports, and the workers there can do what their governments will not. Set it against earlier refusals such as Le Havre, and be plain about what the strike can and cannot stop. Dateline Le Havre.

stories.label: Niger Mass Deaths: Probe panel recommends scholarships for victims' children, N1.4bn compensations
stories.summary: Thirty-three detainees died in September in the custody of Nigeria's Security and Civil Defence Corps in Niger State. The committee that investigated proposes N30 million for each bereaved family, N10 million for each survivor and scholarships for the children, and recommends releasing officers it cleared. Lead with the 33 dead and what the panel found killed them, then the accountability question: who, if anyone, is held responsible, and who was cleared. Nigeria's interior minister received the report, so say what the government has committed to. Dateline Minna if the source supports it.

stories.label: President Erdoğan's noteworthy meeting: He received Bayramov in Aliyev's absence
stories.summary: Azerbaijan's President Aliyev stayed away from the Organization of Turkic States summit after a dispute with Turkey over a headscarf regulation, and Erdoğan received Foreign Minister Bayramov instead. Lead with the absence: the two states that call themselves one nation are openly at odds, over a question of religious dress. Explain the regulation, who it binds and what each side said. The stake: the Turkic bloc's transport corridors, which Tokayev pressed at the same summit, run through Azerbaijan. Dateline Baku.

stories.label: Bengal shifts 12,000 people to safety, Assam monitors situation as GLOF hits adjoining Bhutan
stories.summary: A glacial lake burst in Bhutan's Gasa district, and 12,000 people downstream along the Sankosh River in West Bengal have been moved while Assam watches its vulnerable areas. Lead with the distance: a lake bursting high in one country empties villages in another. The mechanism: warming swells Himalayan glacial lakes held back by unstable moraine, and warning depends on a neighbour's monitoring and how fast it is shared. State any toll in Bhutan as reported, and do not imply one if there is none. Dateline Bhutan or West Bengal as the source supports.

stories.label: ECB's Panetta Says More Rate Hikes May Be Needed to Tame Prices
stories.summary: New development on Thursday's ECB hold: hours later, policymakers opened the rate-hike debate in public, with Bank of Italy governor Panetta saying more increases may be needed, minutes after Italian consumer prices rose more than expected. Reuters reports the Governing Council debated a hike on Thursday before holding, and that an ECB survey sees higher inflation in coming quarters. Lead with the argument inside the bank, not one official's remark. The mechanism: an energy shock from the Iran war raises prices while growth weakens, and the fear is that it spreads into wages. Who pays: indebted governments such as France and households with loans. Name the ECB deposit rate and the euro. Dateline Frankfurt.

stories.label: Bill proposing quarterly gas pricing lands in Senate
stories.summary: A bill tabled in Pakistan's Senate would have natural gas prices set every quarter under an amended Ogra law. Lead with what changes for the household and the factory: bills that move four times a year, in a year when the Iran war has already pushed energy costs up. Explain the current pricing cycle, who gains from faster pass-through (the utilities and the budget) and who carries the risk. Name natural gas prices, and say whether a lender's condition is behind the bill only if the source supports it. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Sudanese leader says Russia could establish free economic zone on Red Sea
stories.summary: State-media only: attribute everything to Russian state news agency TASS. Sudan's army chief al-Burhan has proposed that Russia set up a free economic zone on Sudan's Red Sea coast and help develop its railways. New development after the Russia-Africa summit covered on 29 October, and it follows Moscow's long pursuit of a naval foothold on that coast. Treat Sudan's leadership as the actor: a general at war, whose rule millions of displaced Sudanese live under, is offering coast and rail to a foreign power. Say what he wants in return and what the war means for any such deal. Dateline Port Sudan unless the source says otherwise.

stories.label: British spy agency cannot account for thousands of data storage devices, watchdog says
stories.summary: The UK's Investigatory Powers Commissioner's Office says in its 2025 annual report that GCHQ cannot account for thousands of data storage devices, and that it is 'very concerned' and 'disappointed' at how long the agency has taken to investigate. Lead with the missing devices at the agency that holds bulk surveillance data on people who are suspected of nothing. Say what could be on them, how many there are, and what the watchdog can actually compel. Dateline Cheltenham. A thin feed entry: the IPCO report itself is the primary source if the page will not fetch.

stories.label: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
stories.summary: General Motors will pay $220 million after selling data from its Smart Driver system, marketed as a tool for parents and careful drivers, to brokers who passed it to insurers. Lead with the bait: a safety feature that became a pricing input against the person using it. Say who is paid, how much each owner gets, and whether anyone admitted wrongdoing. The mechanism is the car as a sensor its owner does not control. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Detroit.

stories.label: „Grenzpartnerschaft“: Auch der EU-Datenschützer rügt geplantes Polizeiabkommen mit den USA
stories.summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor is demanding tighter limits on a planned 'border partnership' giving US authorities access to sensitive European police data, with travellers' data the main US aim. Germany's government keeps its negotiating position secret even from parliament. Lead with what Washington would be able to see and what the watchdog objects to. The stake: a condition of visa-free travel becomes a channel for police records, and those whose data moves are not told. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Marine fossils in Colombia reveal possible evolutionary transition without mass extinction
stories.summary: McGill University and Colombia's Centro de Investigaciones Paleontológicas describe a fossil ecosystem in central Colombia where survivors of Jurassic groups overlap with new Cretaceous lineages, a large evolutionary turnover with no mass extinction behind it. Lead with that challenge to the usual story, in which catastrophe clears the way for what comes next. Give the journal, the site and what the overlap shows, and credit the Colombian researchers. Dateline Villa de Leyva if the source names it, otherwise the site it gives. A thin feed entry.
